tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final answer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After solving the puzzle, present the complete sequence of moves as a single list in the exact required format.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the end of reasoning, when you have a full, legal move sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing no moves or an incomplete list, causing the verifier to reject the answer.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Free blocked larger disks by moving top smaller disks first
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk is not the topmost disk on its peg, first move any smaller disks that sit above it to another peg where the move is legal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a larger disk but it is covered by smaller disks on its source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 5 while disk 2 remains on top of it, resulting in a source‑top‑mismatch error.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate destination peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a disk, check that the destination peg is either empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Every time you consider a move, verify the destination legality.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 4 onto a peg whose top disk is disk 2, which is smaller, causing an illegal placement.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate source peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure that the disk you intend to move is the topmost disk on its source peg; moving any other disk is illegal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before executing any move, confirm the source peg's top disk matches the intended disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 5 while disk 2 is on top of it, leading to a source‑top‑mismatch.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Apply classic Hanoi recursion to generate move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When all disks are stacked in correct order on a single source peg and need to be moved to a target peg, use the recursive Hanoi algorithm (move n‑1 to auxiliary, move largest, move n‑1 from auxiliary to target).
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: For sub‑problems that reduce to the classic all‑on‑one‑peg situation.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Failing to use recursion and instead enumerating moves ad‑hoc, leading to a longer or incorrect sequence.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear destination peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg currently holds smaller disks that should be placed above the larger disk in the final order, move those smaller disks elsewhere before moving the larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a larger disk must be placed onto a peg that already contains smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing disk 5 onto a peg that already has disk 1 on top, making the move illegal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Form classic start by moving smallest disk onto full stack
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the larger disks are already correctly stacked on a peg but the smallest disk (or another out‑of‑place disk) is elsewhere, first move that smallest disk onto the full stack to create a classic start configuration.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the puzzle reduces to the classic Hanoi start after handling scattered smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Leaving the smallest disk on a separate peg and trying to apply classic recursion directly, causing an invalid initial state.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Goal‑first descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When the goal is to stack all disks on a single peg, always move the largest remaining disk onto the goal peg first, after clearing any smaller disks from that peg; then repeat for the next largest disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During the final assembly of the stack on the target peg from an arbitrary initial configuration.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a smaller disk onto the goal peg before the larger disks that belong below it, later making it impossible to place the larger disk.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use smallest disk as temporary placeholder
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When a smaller disk blocks a needed move, move the smallest disk (disk 1) to the other peg (if legal) as a temporary placeholder, perform the required larger move, and later move the smallest disk back.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a larger disk cannot be moved because a smaller disk sits on its source or destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Leaving disk 1 on a peg and trying to move disk 2, resulting in a source‑top‑mismatch or illegal placement.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model stops generation before emitting any moves, often due to mis‑parsing the prompt or early termination.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Explicitly generate at least one move; if no moves are needed, output an empty list [] as the move list.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Truncated move list (incomplete solution) due to token limit
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model runs out of generation budget before finishing the full sequence, leaving the list incomplete.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Prefer concise, near‑minimal move sequences and monitor token usage; if the list becomes long, break it into smaller logical chunks or use a more efficient algorithm.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (source peg top mismatch)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model selects a disk that is buried under smaller disks on its source peg, forgetting the rule that only the top disk may be moved.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always check the top of the source peg before choosing a disk to move; if the desired disk is not on top, first relocate the blocking smaller disks.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal placement)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model attempts a move without verifying that the destination peg's top disk is larger, violating the size ordering rule.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate the destination peg before each move; if a smaller disk is on top, move that smaller disk elsewhere first.
